hypothesis: A BUSY caller can request interruption without creating a second Frank presence if the request is an epoch-bound receipt on the one canonical presence lease, and only the exact current holder may acknowledge or decline it.
counterhypothesis: A separate spawn/interrupt state machine or an interrupt request not bound to the observed lease epoch can create split-brain or retarget a stale user intent to a successor holder.

observations: presence BUSY plus spawn IDLE permits contradictory BUSY versus ACQUIRED results

one canonical singleton truth is required

architecture_delta.title: epoch-bound BUSY interrupt handshake
properties: PRESENCE_INTERRUPT_V1 is independently namespaced and does not claim global UnifiedDB V16
request_yield requires the lease_epoch observed in the prior BUSY receipt
holder transition before request yields STALE rather than retargeting
requester session/client refs are persisted as hashes only
only the exact current holder and epoch may ACK or DECLINE
ACK never transfers presence; explicit safe-point release and normal re-acquire remain required
human return while autonomous is classified USER_RETURN_WHILE_AUTONOMOUS
